Run the Array DesignR app

run_app.Rd

Starts the app on the first study area given in areas, or on the bundled Stoney Lake raster when none is given. The app opens on the depth raster with no receivers; click the map or press Generate (20 receivers by default), then press Compute coverage. Stoney Lake, Ontario, is the one bundled lake, offered after the given areas (system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "arraydesignR")). It is a 100 m depth raster derived from the bathymetry made before 2024. The Array DesignR 1.x app came with this raster, and it has the same grid and depths as depth_raster of positionR 1.7.0, with the CRS set to EPSG:32617. It holds 4,818 water cells. Depth is zero or negative metres; 56 of the water cells hold 0. Each area is read once when the app starts.

Usage

run_app(
  areas = NULL,
  options = list(),
  max_water_cells = 250000,
  max_pairs = 1e+06
)

Arguments

areas

A named list of study areas: terra::SpatRaster objects or raster file paths of water depth in metres, with land as NA. The names label them in the app, which opens on the first. With none, the app opens on Stoney Lake.

options

Passed to shiny::shinyApp(), such as list(port = 4321).

max_water_cells

The largest number of water cells a study area, given here or uploaded, may hold.

max_pairs

The largest number of receiver and cell pairs one coverage computation or simulation may take. It must be at least the largest number of water cells among the study areas, which one receiver takes; 4,818 for Stoney Lake alone.

Value

A Shiny app object; printing it runs the app.

Details

A raster in longitude and latitude is projected to the UTM zone of its centre: the standard six-degree zone, 1 to 60, north or south by the centre latitude. The exceptions round Norway and Svalbard are not applied. A raster whose longitudes all lie from 180 to 360 is read as 360 degrees less, and a message says so; a raster that crosses 180 degrees keeps its longitudes and takes the zone of its centre. A raster in longitude and latitude is refused when it spans more than 12 degrees of longitude or 12 degrees of latitude. Its longitudes must lie from -180 to 180 or from 0 to 360, and its latitudes from -90 to 90. A larger area is given as a raster in a projected coordinate reference system in metres, and a lake across 180 degrees in the 0 to 360 form. A projected raster is refused when its scale at the raster centre, on its two axes or its diagonals, is more than 1 percent from 1. It is also refused when that scale cannot be measured, as in a local engineering CRS with no geographic datum.

Coverage is computed as a shiny::ExtendedTask through promises::future_promise(). Under the default sequential future plan the computation runs in the app's own R process. Set future::plan(future::multisession) before calling run_app() to run it in a background process, so one user's computation does not hold up another's; the deployed app does this in its app.R.

Two limits keep one computation within the memory of a small server. A study area given to run_app() or uploaded may hold at most max_water_cells water cells; the bundled lake is not limited. One computation may take at most max_pairs receiver and cell pairs, counted two ways. Coverage counts only the pairs within the distance at which the detection curve falls below 0.001. The simulation counts every receiver and water-cell pair, since an animal can be in any water cell. Set the limits from the memory of the server the app runs on.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  run_app()
}
